newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends 0.17 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends 0.17 pct higher.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed 0.17 percent higher on Thursday driven by banks, credit firms and oil refinery Samir, brokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 639.44 points from 638.33 points on Wednesday.
"Technical corrections in the biggest capitalisation firms make them very interesting to buy but shareholders are still cautious," a broker at BMCI Securities said.

Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur (BMCE) rose 18 dirhams to 629 dirhams and Wafabank five dirhams to 800 dirhams. Banque Commerciale du Maroc fell 13 dirhams to 855 dirhams and Banque Marocaine du Commerce et de l'Industrie slipped to 481 dirhams, down nine dirhams.
Credit firm Credor jumped 43 dirhams to 766 dirhams, Eqdom Credit advanced to 1,058 dirhams, up 30 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir was up 10.6 dirhams to 367.00 dirhams.
Both issues of privatisation bonds, gained respectively 21 and 36 dirhams to 1,420 and 1,248 dirhams ahead of the flotation of 20 percent of Imiter silver mine.
Subscriptions will be open from June 9-13. The bonds which give holders prefential options on equity in privatisable firms, were issued respectively in January and April 1996.
Morocco's large private conglomerate ONA Group edged down two dirhams to 780 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, another big private conglomerate, dropped eight dirhams to 730 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid edged up two dirhams to 565 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 49.2 million dirhams versus 63 million on Wednesday.
On the over-the-counter market, volume totalled 56 million dirhams from 63 million dirhams. Main trade was in BMCE shares.
